name: webhooks
description: Verify and sign webhooks: GitHub, Stripe, Slack, Standard Webhooks, Shopify and custom HMAC schemes, with timestamp tolerance and replay protection

api.name: WebhookErr
api.sig: pub type WebhookErr = MissingHeader{name: Str} | MalformedHeader{name: Str, why: Str} | SignatureMismatch | TooOld{age: Int, tolerance: Int} | TooNew{ahead: Int, tolerance: Int} | Replayed{id: Str} | InvalidKey{why: Str} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
Why a webhook was refused. No variant carries the expected signature, so an error can be
logged or returned without helping an attacker.

api.name: Algorithm
api.sig: pub type Algorithm = Sha256 | Sha512 derive Eq, Show
api.doc: The HMAC hash function of a scheme.

api.name: Encoding
api.sig: pub type Encoding = Hex | Base64 | Base64Url derive Eq, Show
api.doc: How a signature is written as text: lower-case hex, padded base64 or unpadded base64url.

api.name: text_key
api.sig: fn text_key(s: Secret[Str]) -> Secret[Bytes]
api.doc: A shared secret given as text (the usual form in provider dashboards), as an HMAC key.

api.name: hmac
api.sig: fn hmac(alg: Algorithm, key: Secret[Bytes], data: Str) -> Bytes
api.doc: The HMAC of `data` under `key` with `alg`.

api.name: encode
api.sig: fn encode(e: Encoding, b: Bytes) -> Str
api.doc: `b` written with encoding `e`.

api.name: decode
api.sig: fn decode(e: Encoding, s: Str) -> Opt[Bytes]
api.doc:
The bytes `s` encodes with `e`, or none when it is not valid in that encoding. Hex accepts
either case.

api.name: matches
api.sig: fn matches(alg: Algorithm, e: Encoding, keys: List[Secret[Bytes]], data: Str, given: Str) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether the encoded signature `given` is the HMAC of `data` under one of `keys`. Every key is
tried and each comparison is constant time, so the time taken doesn't say which bytes or which
key matched.

api.name: unix_now
api.sig: fn unix_now() -> Int ! time
api.doc: The current Unix time in seconds, for the `now` parameters.

api.name: parse_timestamp
api.sig: fn parse_timestamp(s: Str) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc: A Unix timestamp in seconds as a header carries it: 1 to 12 ASCII digits, nothing else.

api.name: check_timestamp
api.sig: fn check_timestamp(ts: Int, now: Int, tolerance: Int where _ >= 0) -> Res[Unit, WebhookErr]
api.doc:
Whether `ts` is within `tolerance` seconds of `now`, in either direction. A tolerance of 0
disables the check.

api.name: default_tolerance
api.sig: fn default_tolerance() -> Int
api.doc: The default tolerance of Stripe, Slack and Standard Webhooks: 5 minutes.

api.name: github_signature
api.sig: fn github_signature(key: Secret[Bytes], body: Str) -> Str
api.doc: The value of `X-Hub-Signature-256` for `body`: `sha256=` and the hex HMAC-SHA-256.

api.name: github_headers
api.sig: fn github_headers(key: Secret[Bytes], body: Str) -> List[(Str, Str)]
api.doc: The headers a sender adds to a GitHub-style delivery of `body`.

api.name: github_verify
api.sig: fn github_verify(keys: List[Secret[Bytes]] where _.len > 0, body: Str, header: Str) -> Res[Unit, WebhookErr]
api.doc:
Checks an `X-Hub-Signature-256` value against `body` and any of `keys`. The legacy SHA-1
`X-Hub-Signature` header is not accepted.

api.name: github_verify_request
api.sig: fn github_verify_request(keys: List[Secret[Bytes]] where _.len > 0, req: Request) -> Res[Unit, WebhookErr]
api.doc:
Checks a GitHub delivery received by an `http.serve` handler: its raw body and its
`X-Hub-Signature-256` header.

api.name: StripeHeader
api.sig: pub type StripeHeader = {timestamp: Int, v1: List[Str]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A parsed `Stripe-Signature` header: the timestamp and every `v1` signature. Other schemes,
such as the test-mode `v0`, are ignored.

api.name: stripe_parse
api.sig: fn stripe_parse(header: Str) -> Res[StripeHeader, WebhookErr]
api.doc:
Parses `t=<seconds>,v1=<hex>[,v1=<hex>...]`. A header without exactly one valid `t`, without
a `v1`, with an element that isn't `key=value`, or with more than 20 elements is malformed.

api.name: stripe_signature
api.sig: fn stripe_signature(key: Secret[Bytes], body: Str, timestamp: Int where _ >= 0) -> Str
api.doc:
The `v1` signature of `body` sent at `timestamp`: hex HMAC-SHA-256 of `"{timestamp}.{body}"`.
Stripe's endpoint secrets (`whsec_...`) are used as text, prefix included: `text_key`.

api.name: stripe_test_header
api.sig: fn stripe_test_header(key: Secret[Bytes], body: Str, timestamp: Int where _ >= 0) -> Str
api.doc:
A `Stripe-Signature` value for `body` at `timestamp`, as stripe-node's
`generateTestHeaderString` makes, for tests and for senders.

api.name: stripe_verify
api.sig: fn stripe_verify(keys: List[Secret[Bytes]] where _.len > 0, body: Str, header: Str, now: Int, tolerance: Int where _ >= 0) -> Res[Unit, WebhookErr]
api.doc:
Checks a `Stripe-Signature` value: one of its `v1` signatures must match under one of `keys`,
and its timestamp must be within `tolerance` seconds of `now` (0 disables the check).

api.name: stripe_verify_request
api.sig: fn stripe_verify_request(keys: List[Secret[Bytes]] where _.len > 0, req: Request, now: Int, tolerance: Int where _ >= 0) -> Res[Unit, WebhookErr]
api.doc: Checks a Stripe event received by an `http.serve` handler.

api.name: slack_signature
api.sig: fn slack_signature(key: Secret[Bytes], timestamp: Int where _ >= 0, body: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
The `X-Slack-Signature` value for `body` sent at `timestamp`: `v0=` and the hex
HMAC-SHA-256 of `"v0:{timestamp}:{body}"`.

api.name: slack_headers
api.sig: fn slack_headers(key: Secret[Bytes], timestamp: Int where _ >= 0, body: Str) -> List[(Str, Str)]
api.doc: The headers Slack sends with a request: the timestamp and the signature.

api.name: slack_verify
api.sig: fn slack_verify(keys: List[Secret[Bytes]] where _.len > 0, body: Str, timestamp: Str, signature: Str, now: Int, tolerance: Int where _ >= 0) -> Res[Unit, WebhookErr]
api.doc:
Checks a Slack request given its `X-Slack-Request-Timestamp` and `X-Slack-Signature`
values. The timestamp is checked first, as Slack recommends, against `tolerance` seconds.

api.name: slack_verify_request
api.sig: fn slack_verify_request(keys: List[Secret[Bytes]] where _.len > 0, req: Request, now: Int) -> Res[Unit, WebhookErr]
api.doc: Checks a Slack request received by an `http.serve` handler, with Slack's 5 minute window.

api.name: StandardHeaders
api.sig: pub type StandardHeaders = {id: Str, timestamp: Str, signature: Str} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: The three headers of the Standard Webhooks specification, as received.

api.name: standard_key
api.sig: fn standard_key(s: Secret[Str]) -> Res[Secret[Bytes], WebhookErr]
api.doc:
A symmetric Standard Webhooks secret, `whsec_` and base64 (the prefix is optional), as an
HMAC key. The specification requires 24 to 64 bytes.

api.name: standard_public_key
api.sig: fn standard_public_key(s: Str) -> Res[Bytes, WebhookErr]
api.doc: A Standard Webhooks Ed25519 public key, `whpk_` and the base64 of 32 bytes (prefix optional).

api.name: standard_content
api.sig: fn standard_content(id: Str, timestamp: Int, body: Str) -> Str
api.doc: The content every Standard Webhooks signature covers: `"{id}.{timestamp}.{body}"`.

api.name: standard_signature
api.sig: fn standard_signature(key: Secret[Bytes], id: Str, timestamp: Int where _ >= 0, body: Str) -> Str
api.doc: A `v1,<base64>` symmetric signature of a message.

api.name: standard_signature_ed25519
api.sig: fn standard_signature_ed25519(sk: Secret[Bytes], id: Str, timestamp: Int where _ >= 0, body: Str) -> Str
api.doc: A `v1a,<base64>` Ed25519 signature of a message, under the 32-byte secret seed `sk`.

api.name: standard_headers
api.sig: fn standard_headers(key: Secret[Bytes], id: Str where _.len > 0, timestamp: Int where _ >= 0, body: Str) -> List[(Str, Str)]
api.doc: The three headers a sender adds, with one `v1` signature.

api.name: standard_signatures
api.sig: fn standard_signatures(header: Str, v: Str) -> Res[List[Str], WebhookErr]
api.doc:
The signatures of a `webhook-signature` value with version `v`: the list is space separated,
each entry `version,base64`, and other versions are skipped.

api.name: standard_verify
api.sig: fn standard_verify(keys: List[Secret[Bytes]] where _.len > 0, h: StandardHeaders, body: Str, now: Int, tolerance: Int where _ >= 0) -> Res[Unit, WebhookErr]
api.doc:
Checks a message signed with symmetric keys: the timestamp within `tolerance` seconds of
`now`, then a `v1` signature under one of `keys`.

api.name: standard_verify_ed25519
api.sig: fn standard_verify_ed25519(pks: List[Bytes] where _.len > 0, h: StandardHeaders, body: Str, now: Int, tolerance: Int where _ >= 0) -> Res[Unit, WebhookErr]
api.doc: Checks a message signed with Ed25519 (`v1a`) against any of the public keys `pks`.

api.name: standard_headers_of
api.sig: fn standard_headers_of(req: Request) -> Res[StandardHeaders, WebhookErr]
api.doc: The Standard Webhooks headers of a request, or the first one missing.

api.name: standard_verify_request
api.sig: fn standard_verify_request(keys: List[Secret[Bytes]] where _.len > 0, req: Request, now: Int, tolerance: Int where _ >= 0) -> Res[Unit, WebhookErr]
api.doc: Checks a symmetric Standard Webhooks message received by an `http.serve` handler.

api.name: shopify_signature
api.sig: fn shopify_signature(key: Secret[Bytes], body: Str) -> Str
api.doc: The `X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256` value for `body`: the base64 HMAC-SHA-256.

api.name: shopify_verify
api.sig: fn shopify_verify(keys: List[Secret[Bytes]] where _.len > 0, body: Str, header: Str) -> Res[Unit, WebhookErr]
api.doc: Checks an `X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256` value against `body` and any of `keys`.

api.name: shopify_verify_request
api.sig: fn shopify_verify_request(keys: List[Secret[Bytes]] where _.len > 0, req: Request) -> Res[Unit, WebhookErr]
api.doc: Checks a Shopify webhook received by an `http.serve` handler.

api.name: Signed
api.sig: pub type Signed = BodyOnly | Timestamped{header: Str where _.len > 0, lead: Str, sep: Str, tolerance: Int where _ >= 0} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
What a scheme signs: the body alone, or `lead + timestamp + sep + body` with the timestamp
(Unix seconds) taken from the header `header` and checked against `tolerance` seconds (0
disables the check). Slack's scheme is `Timestamped{header: "x-slack-request-timestamp",
lead: "v0:", sep: ":", tolerance: 300}`.

api.name: Scheme
api.sig: pub type Scheme = {header: Str where _.len > 0, prefix: Str, algorithm: Algorithm, encoding: Encoding, separator: Str, signed: Signed} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A custom HMAC scheme: the signature is in `header` as `prefix` and the encoded HMAC of the
signed content. Several signatures may be sent separated by `separator` (`""` for one).

api.name: hmac_scheme
api.sig: fn hmac_scheme(header: Str where _.len > 0) -> Scheme
api.doc:
A scheme with the common defaults: HMAC-SHA-256 of the body, hex, no prefix, one signature in
`header`. Change fields with `with`.

api.name: scheme_content
api.sig: fn scheme_content(s: Scheme, timestamp: Int, body: Str) -> Str
api.doc: The content `s` signs for `body` sent at `timestamp` (ignored for `BodyOnly`).

api.name: scheme_signature
api.sig: fn scheme_signature(s: Scheme, key: Secret[Bytes], timestamp: Int where _ >= 0, body: Str) -> Str
api.doc: The signature header value under `s` for `body` sent at `timestamp`.

api.name: scheme_headers
api.sig: fn scheme_headers(s: Scheme, key: Secret[Bytes], timestamp: Int where _ >= 0, body: Str) -> List[(Str, Str)]
api.doc: The headers a sender adds under `s`: the signature, and the timestamp when the scheme signs one.

api.name: scheme_verify
api.sig: fn scheme_verify(s: Scheme, keys: List[Secret[Bytes]] where _.len > 0, headers: List[(Str, Str)], body: Str, now: Int) -> Res[Unit, WebhookErr]
api.doc:
Checks a message under `s`, given the headers it came with (names compared without regard to
case) and its raw body.

api.name: scheme_verify_request
api.sig: fn scheme_verify_request(s: Scheme, keys: List[Secret[Bytes]] where _.len > 0, req: Request, now: Int) -> Res[Unit, WebhookErr]
api.doc: Checks a request received by an `http.serve` handler under `s`.

api.name: Seen
api.sig: pub type Seen = {until: Map[Str, Int]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
Delivery ids seen recently, each with the Unix second it may be forgotten at. An immutable
value for one thread or one process loop; use the SQLite store to share it between handlers.

api.name: seen_empty
api.sig: fn seen_empty() -> Seen
api.doc: No ids seen.

api.name: seen_purge
api.sig: fn seen_purge(s: Seen, now: Int) -> Seen
api.doc: `s` without the ids whose time ran out by `now`.

api.name: seen_claim
api.sig: fn seen_claim(s: Seen, id: Str where _.len > 0, now: Int, ttl: Int where _ > 0) -> (Res[Unit, WebhookErr], Seen)
api.doc:
Claims `id` at `now` for `ttl` seconds: `ok` and the updated set the first time, `Replayed`
while an earlier claim is live. Expired ids are dropped as it goes. Use a `ttl` at least the
timestamp tolerance, so a replay can't outlive its claim and still pass the timestamp check.

api.name: replay_setup
api.sig: fn replay_setup(c: Db) -> Unit ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Creates the SQLite table of claimed ids, `webhooks_seen`, if it isn't there.

api.name: replay_claim
api.sig: fn replay_claim(c: Db, id: Str where _.len > 0, now: Int, ttl: Int where _ > 0) -> Res[Unit, WebhookErr] ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc:
Claims `id` in the database at `now` for `ttl` seconds, atomically: of any number of handlers
or processes claiming one id at once, exactly one gets `ok`. An expired claim can be taken
again.

api.name: replay_purge
api.sig: fn replay_purge(c: Db, now: Int) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Deletes the claims that ran out by `now`, and gives how many went.
